children: Condor’s Q3 2026 Uzbekistan production averaged 16,693 boe/d, up 20% from Q2 2026 and 67% from Q3 2025. In October, it completed a $72.03M convertible debenture offering at 12% annual interest.
Material Details
Detail
AI Analyst View
Q3 production averaged 16,693 boe/d
Production rose 20% QoQ and 67% YoY, showing significant operating growth; disclosed volumes cover the PEC Project, with 51% attributable to Condor.
Raised $72.03M in convertible debentures
Funds support compressor and LNG projects, but the 12% coupon adds cash interest costs and conversion may dilute shareholders.
Debentures convert at $6.00/share; mature Oct. 15, 2029
The conversion price defines potential dilution; the release gives no comparison with the current share price.
A-22 test averaged 6.0 MMscf/d over 8 hours
Could expand prospective drilling at Andakli, but the company cautions the short-term test may not indicate long-term performance or recovery.
Compressor could add up to 30 MMscf/d
The modeled production uplift could be material, but it is an estimate; commissioning is scheduled for Q2 2027.
First LNG Facility completion needs USD $21.0M more
The remaining construction and commissioning cost requires funding; the company is reviewing third-party financing alternatives.
Context by AI Analyst

This is an operating-growth update alongside ongoing development of Condor’s Uzbekistan gas business and Kazakhstan LNG project. Next, traders will look for reported financial results, follow-up well testing, compressor commissioning and secured funding for LNG construction.
